items.title: The Trinity:Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents
items.summary: Multimodal intelligence can be viewed as human-guided co-evolution between worlds and agents through interaction. However, scaling this process faces two bottlenecks: constructing heterogeneous, verifiable environments is costly, and manual Harness iteration cannot keep pace with growing task diversity and complexity. items.summary: Training a spatial VLM to answer which side an object lies on does not require it to preserve the metric displacement that determines that answer, while supervision for a distance estimate may leave categorical relations largely unconstrained. items.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
items.summary: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but their understanding of physical dynamics remains limited. items.title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
items.summary: Interactive world generation requires models to follow successive commands while preserving relevant history and action consequences. We present Hy-Nomas, a video world model with an 8B diffusion backbone that supports free-form text instructions and continuous camera control across multiple interaction turns. items.title: VibeVideoBench: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation
items.summary: Diffusion video models produce striking clips, but they cannot reliably render an exact formula, a correct chart, a rule-consistent game or narration synchronized to on-screen events. A different route is emerging: multimodal agents that write code to render every frame and synthesize every sound. items.summary: Discrete visual tokens represent vision in a discrete form analogous to language, offering a native interface for multimodal modeling under a shared next-token prediction objective. items.title: HABIT-Bench: Evaluating Habit Induction from Longitudinal Weak Evidence in Agent Memory
items.summary: In long-term interactions with large language model (LLM) agents, users reveal habits through their choices and actions. These habits capture implicit user information that agents must infer across conversations. However, individual observations may provide only partial evidence about a habit or when it applies. items.title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
items.summary: Memory is increasingly used in long-horizon agents, yet the net value of building memory over direct retrieval from raw history remains largely unclear. Through a large-scale evaluation across multiple benchmarks and model backbones, we find many dedicated memory systems underperform naive RAG in many cases, indicating a negative net value. items.title: Multiscale Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.summary: Long-horizon LLM agents interact with their environments through complete assistant turns while generating each action token by token. items.title: Representation Redistribution in Sparse Autoencoders
items.summary: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) decompose language model activations into sparse features, but prompt transformations designed to preserve the underlying request can redistribute activity across them. items.summary: Recent test-time training (TTT) frameworks have enabled open-weight large language models (LLMs) to outperform inference-only frameworks powered by frontier models on scientific discovery tasks. items.title: Rollback: Experience Backtracking in World Models for Policy Improvement
items.summary: Action-conditioned world models offer a scalable alternative to costly real-world interaction for improving robot policies. However, existing world-model-based methods largely treat world models as forward-only surrogates of the physical environment, leaving untapped a capability no physical environment affords: rewinding to past decision points to explore counterfactual futures. items.title: CodeCap-Bench: Can Code Serve as a Good Video Caption?
items.summary: Video captioning aims to preserve visual information through compact descriptions, predominantly using natural language. items.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have made substantial progress in robotic manipulation, but their generalization remains constrained by the diversity and coverage of action-labeled robot demonstrations. items.title: OvisOCR3 Technical Report
items.summary: We introduce OvisOCR3, a 0.8B model for a broad range of OCR-related tasks. OvisOCR3 unifies document parsing, general OCR, key information extraction (KIE), document figure captioning, and cross-page table reconstruction in a single model. items.title: LociArt: A Unified Paradigm for Free-Style Local Video Stylization
items.summary: Video stylization typically transforms entire scenes, while local artistic editing requires precise region--style association, spatial control, and temporal consistency. items.title: Truncate or Not? A Scaling Study of Looped Transformers with Truncated Backpropagation
items.summary: Looped transformers reuse a shared block of layers to increase computational depth without increasing the number of trainable parameters. They are trained with backpropagation through time (BPTT). items.title: On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit-Order Prediction
items.summary: Diffusion language models (DLMs) promise parallel text generation, but in practice face an unresolved speed-quality trade-off. Exact decoding fills in only one masked position per model pass, while faster multi-token decoding schemes are lossy. items.title: Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception
items.summary: Multimodal perception forms the foundation of multimodal intelligence. In particular, spatial perception and multimodal long-context understanding are two pivotal tasks that underpin embodied AI and multimodal agents. items.title: RSI Arena: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement with Human Feedback
items.summary: Can AI agents autonomously train useful language models and improve them using feedback from users? We introduce RSI Arena, a two-stage study of autonomous post-training as a step toward recursive self-improvement. items.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are bottlenecked by loading routed-expert weights from memory during interactive decoding at small batch sizes. items.title: MatAnyone-E: Sparse Memory Propagation for Efficient High-Resolution Video Matting
items.summary: High-resolution video matting requires preserving fine details, such as hair strands and soft transparency, while maintaining consistency across frames. items.title: What Effort Level Should I Choose? On the Economics of Reasoning Effort in LLM Agents
items.summary: Generative models increasingly expose a reasoning effort setting that lets users scale inference-time compute, trading higher cost for potentially improved performance. items.title: How Far Can Coding Agents Go in Visual Generation?
items.summary: Modern image generation largely relies on specialized generative models that leave the process of image construction implicit in learned parameters.
